newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Monday with most traders sidelined due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives, dealers said.
The market is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday and Wednesday, they said.

"Rates were steady to higher in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for more clues to monetary policy from Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins speech," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday was unchanged from last Friday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent.
Tuesday/Wednesday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, nine-months was unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
